:::{#rem-loocv}
#### When to use leave-one-out cross-validation

LOOCV is the $\nfolds = \nobs$ end of @rem-choosing-k.
By @rem-cv-estimate, $\cvest{\nobs}$ estimates $\expgenerr{\fitproc}{\nobs - 1}$ for the fitting procedure $\fitproc$:
each rule is fitted to $\nobs - 1$ observations,
so the bias of $\cvest{\nobs}$ as an estimate of $\expgenerr{\fitproc}{\nobs}$ is the smallest of any $\nfolds$.
But the $\nobs$ training sets are nearly identical,
so the variance of $\cvest{\nobs}$ can be larger than that of 5- or 10-fold cross-validation
[@james2021islr2e, sec. 5.1.4].
For least squares fits,
@thm-loocv-shortcut computes LOOCV from a single fit;
for most other fitting methods,
LOOCV requires $\nobs$ fits.

:::
